original.reason: Step 2 is invalid: from f(y^2)=0 for all nonzero y one obtains only that f vanishes on (0,∞), not on negative inputs. No oddness has been proved, so the asserted conclusion f≡0 and hence the unique-zero claim are unsupported.

judgment.reason: Its replacement proof of the unique-zero claim has a material gap. The assertion that substituting tail zeros into P 'forces f(x)=0' is neither specified nor derived.
The lemma is not proved rigorously: the crucial claim that an opposite-sign substitution forces f(x)=0 is asserted without an equation or argument establishing it.
The proof of the zero-set claim contains the same unsupported leap from vanishing on tails to f(x)=0. Since later steps depend on this claim, the proof is incomplete.
The central implication in the claim—tail vanishing 'forces f(x)=0' after another substitution—is not demonstrated. This is a material gap in the unique-zero argument.
